title: Task tests manifest, version 1
description: Produced by a project, read by rEngine, keyed by the task key the project's own tracker provider uses (F123, BAS-1020, #42). rEngine joins on that key and never parses its meaning. An entry with no sabotage rows is UNPROVEN however green its last run was: AGENTS.md defines a regression as established only once observed failing for its own reason, and a passing command is not that. A run's artifacts are declared rather than guessed at from what `log` points to (spec 126). See docs/specs/117-task-tests-manifest.md.

version.description: Bumped when the entry shape changes, so an older reader says "unknown version" rather than misreading.

at.description: When the manifest was produced. Shown, never compared to now.

commit.description: The revision it was produced at, so a reader can say whether it describes the checkout in front of them.

task.description: The provider's own task key. Not parsed.

path.description: Root-relative path to the test. Never opened by this reader.

name.description: How the runner selects it: a test name, ctest name or grep tag.

claim.description: One sentence saying what the test asserts, in the project's own words.

criteria.description: Which of the task's acceptance criteria this test backs, 1-based. Checked against the task where the provider knows its criteria; a claim pointing past them reads as coverage the task does not have.

tier.description: The project's own tier word: gate, slow, deployed, manual. Not interpreted, only shown and grouped.

preconditions.description: What must be present for it to run at all: game data, a device, a token, a flag.

break.description: The specific edit that was made to the implementation.

red.description: What went red because of it, and for its own reason rather than something earlier.

sabotage.description: The evidence that the test bites. An entry without these is unproven; this is the field the whole format exists for.

result.description: What the project last saw. A claim about a run, never about the task.

log.description: Where the project kept the output. Not opened.

artifacts.description: What the run produced that is worth looking at: a rendered frame, a diff image, a report. Root-relative paths the project wrote. rEngine opens one when asked and produces, refreshes and regenerates nothing — `log` stays the text output it always was, because "where the output went" and "what the run produced" are different claims and one field cannot make both.

path.description: Root-relative. A path that escapes the project root is refused by name and never opened.

label.description: What it is, in the project's own words. Shown in place of the file name when given.
